likely_bugs.spec_basis: "The variable counts as enabled when its value, trimmed of surrounding whitespace and compared case-insensitively, is one of "1", "true" or "yes". For example, "1", "true", "TRUE", "True", "YES" and " yes " all enable it."
likely_bugs.reason: The spec lists "True" by name as a value that enables MAE coordinate descent, so no warning should be emitted when SGTLEARN_MAE_CD=True. The implementation compares the raw value exactly against {"1", "true", "TRUE", "yes"}, without trimming or lowercasing it first, so "True" (and also "YES" and " yes ") are treated as disabled and the warning fires anyway. The test asserts what the spec requires.

suspicions.analysis:
Logical mistakes: The opt-in environment variable check is inconsistent about case. The criterion is normalized (whitespace stripped, lowercased) before comparison, but SGTLEARN_MAE_CD is compared exactly against a fixed set. "1", "true", "TRUE" and "yes" count as enabled, while "True", "YES", "Yes" or " true " do not. Accepting both "true" and "TRUE" shows the check is meant to be case-insensitive. As written, a user who sets SGTLEARN_MAE_CD=True or SGTLEARN_MAE_CD=YES has turned the feature on but still gets the "disabled" warning.
Robustness omissions: Surrounding whitespace in the environment variable value is not stripped, so a value such as "1 " or "yes\n" (common in shell or .env files) is treated as disabled. The criterion itself is handled safely: non-string or None values are converted to text and never match. Nothing else is missing. The function should never raise.
